name: Longest log with capped repeats
brief:
A market-data audit reads a log of message ids, `log`. A stretch of consecutive entries is clean when no id appears in it more than `m` times.

Write `longest_capped_run(log, m)`, which returns the length of the longest clean stretch, or 0 for an empty log.

Example. For `log = ['a', 'b', 'a', 'a', 'c', 'b']` and `m = 2`, the stretch `'a', 'a', 'c', 'b'` holds `'a'` twice and is clean. The first five entries hold `'a'` three times. The answer is 4.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$ entries, each a string; $1 \le m \le n$ when the log is not empty.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Starting a fresh count at every position is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep a count of each id inside the window. When the new entry pushes its own count past `m`, move the left edge on until that count is back to `m`.

examples.note: The last four entries hold each id at most twice.
With `m = 1` any two neighbouring `'x'` entries already break the cap.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Only the newest entry can push a count past `m`, so the window shrinks until that one id is back under the cap.
Jumping the left edge to just after the last copy of the id works only for `m = 1`; for larger `m` it drops too much.
Each entry enters the window once and leaves at most once, so the work is $O(n)$.

planted.slip: Jumping past the last copy of the id treats every cap as 1.
Shrinking while a count is `>= m` refuses a stretch that holds an id exactly `m` times.
Lowering the new id's count instead of the count of the entry that leaves leaves stale counts in the window.
